compiled_state.title: As a maintainer, I want query-stats.sh with 5 validation subcommands plus /dso:review-stats --source=central dispatcher wiring, so that I can validate the central telemetry store and answer cross-reviewer questions.
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Implement `plugins/dso/scripts/telemetry/query-stats.sh` using bash + AWS CLI + DuckDB, providing 5 subcommands: `roundtrip` (emit test event and verify it lands in S3), `counts` (events per tool_id × event_type × day), `recent` (latest N events), `missing` (date partitions with zero events), `sizes` (bytes per client_id). Unknown subcommand exits 1 with usage. Add `--source=central` flag to `/dso:review-stats` skill that dispatches `query-stats.sh`.
**Why**: This is the read-side of the telemetry pipeline — without it operators cannot validate the bucket or answer cross-reviewer questions.
**Scope**:
- IN: `query-stats.sh` with 5 subcommands, unknown-subcommand exit 1, `/dso:review-stats --source=central` dispatcher wiring, date-range partitioning.
- OUT: Full analytics dashboards or reporting UI (downstream epics). Backfill of historical data.

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, `query-stats.sh roundtrip` emits a test event to the configured endpoint and confirms it lands in S3, exiting 0 on success.
  ← Satisfies: sc-2, sc-7  (sc-2: "query-stats.sh roundtrip verifies S3 landing"; sc-7: "5 subcommands including roundtrip")
- When this story is complete, `query-stats.sh counts`, `recent`, `missing`, and `sizes` each produce non-error output against a populated S3 bucket using AWS CLI and DuckDB with date-range partitioning (not a full-bucket scan).
  ← Satisfies: sc-7  (sc-7: "query-stats.sh provides 5 subcommands via AWS CLI + DuckDB with date-range partitioning")
- When this story is complete, `query-stats.sh` invoked with an unknown subcommand exits 1 and prints a usage message listing the 5 valid subcommands.
  ← Satisfies: sc-7
- When this story is complete, running `/dso:review-stats --source=central` dispatches `query-stats.sh` and surfaces its output.
  ← Satisfies: sc-7

## Considerations

- [DuckDB credential configuration] DuckDB requires either AWS credentials in the environment/.aws (httpfs extension reads from env) or an explicit CREATE SECRET statement. Document which mechanism `query-stats.sh` uses and how to configure it on a fresh checkout. Queries must source the same AWS profile as `aws-status.sh` and `aws-verify-live.sh`.
- [Date partition] Queries must use date-range partitioning on the `YYYY-MM-DD` key prefix (e.g., `--days=7` glob) to avoid full-bucket scans. Document the required flag.
- [DuckDB version] DuckDB v1.5.3 is the assumed runtime; document this in the script header.
- [Roundtrip] The roundtrip subcommand should use a unique test `client_id` (e.g., `dso-roundtrip-test`) to avoid polluting production-stats queries.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
